claim.summary: For a connected graph side S in a maximum-degree-Delta>=2 graph, k>=2Delta boundary edges and arbitrary F3 charges, any private spanning-tree flow with all chords zero uniquely solves the side on its boundary-charge promise. Common substitution preserves Boolean/parity operations and reuse, but some substituted private edge indicator realizes MOD3-zero on floor(k/(2Delta)) Boolean bits by constant-size boundary substitutions lying entirely in that promise. Weighted tree-centroid proof. Every connected bounded-degree n>=4 graph has a proof-independent connected bipartition with both sides >=n/(2Delta); uniform expansion then gives k=Omega(n). Generic literalwise fixed-depth flow substitution is therefore impossible at polynomial size. Separate existential projections also fail MP when an internal cycle supplies different private witnesses.
claim.assessment: Working all-parameter graph/weighted-tree and exact Boolean restriction proof, medium reviewed. Credits the old connected-side projection and circuit theorem. This tests a generic semantic normalization, not extraction from arbitrary Frege, not all proof-dependent witness choices, and not old PC quotient evaluation.

claim.summary: For every r>=2, ternary one-hot Tseitin on the 2r-vertex ladder with rails oriented forward, rungs left-to-right, charge1 only at last right vertex, has O(r)-line width<=15 resolution-with-weakening refutations, hence polynomial-size constant-depth Frege refutations in the unbounded-fan-in Boolean presentation. Splitting into left/right connected rails gives shared-rung projections sumx=0 and sumx=2 overF3. Any separator I=1 on the first and0 on the second yields Boolean MOD3-zero by I(u,0) AND NOT I(u,2), despite the unpromised third residue. Smolensky therefore forbids polynomial-size fixed-depth AC0[2] separators. Ladder expansion<=1/floor(r/2), so this refutes only an all-Tseitin extractor, not the candidate expander-specific one.
claim.assessment: Working actual-graph refinement of the earlier running-counter control, medium reviewed after specifying the unbounded-fan-in discharge convention. Full local assignment-tree resolution proof and two-copy reduction supplied. GAP checks33792 fixed local Boolean assignments with expected premise/negative-control totals; this is not a graph-size extrapolation. Circuit lower bound is the established primary Smolensky Theorem2.

claim.summary: On an n>=4 graph of edge expansion epsilon>0 with nonzero total F3 charge, any refutation of vertex equations by scalar multiplication and binary linear combination has a line with vertex potential support in[n/3,2n/3) and at least epsilon*n/6 nonzero edge coefficients. The final potential is a nonzero constant; the first large support is the union of two smaller ones, and a nonzero level-set cut gives expansion. For fixed-degree constant-expansion families, exact fixed-depth AC0[2] circuits for all such line predicates on the whole valid one-hot cube must include a superpolynomial-size line, by fixing one active edge and reducing to MOD3 on Omega(n) bits. This is a restricted charge-derivation representation lower bound; extraction from arbitrary Frege is unproved.
claim.assessment: Working all-parameter balanced-support proof and circuit restriction, medium reviewed. DAG reuse and cancellations are allowed. No claim that general Frege lines are charge equations, no new circuit lower bound, and no PC-degree conclusion. Compatible with the older balanced character-cut upper proof.

claim.summary: For every integer r>=1 of ternary labels, the zero-sum predicate is e0^T product_i S^(x_i) e0 for the three-cycle matrix S, hence has tensor-train bond at most three and polynomial-size O(1+log r)-depth Boolean circuits by balanced residue addition. Restriction to binary labels is MOD3, so neither resource implies small fixed-depth AC0[2] circuits. The diagonal two-qutrit disjunction x1=0 or x2=0 has rank five and is not one stabilizer-code projector, whose rank divides nine.
claim.assessment: Elementary classical representation controls, medium reviewed, not new circuit lower bounds. Qutrit rank test reuses the prior binary stabilizer-parity mechanism. Complex stabilizer objects are not identified with the finite-field charged quotient.
